meta.title: AgentScope | Understand and Verify Agent Failures
meta.description: Explain why an AI agent failed, create a safe new attempt and verify the fix with execution evidence.
meta.openGraphDescription: A guided AI product case from failed agent outcome to safe recovery and verified fix.
meta.socialAlt: AgentScope guided product flow from failed agent run to verified fix
header.description: HarnessLab Agent black box for trace replay, failure inspection and evaluation.
language.label: Language
home.title: Understand why an agent failed. Verify what fixes it.
home.description: AgentScope turns a failed agent run into a clear, evidence-backed path from problem to verified fix.
home.previewCaption: A guided path from failure to verified fix
home.problemTitle: A final answer is not enough to debug an agent
home.problemDescription: When an agent fails, teams need to know where progress stopped, what changed and whether the next attempt actually improved the outcome.
home.primaryUserTitle: Built for teams shipping agent-powered products
home.primaryUserDescription: The primary user needs a fast way to explain a failed run, choose a safe recovery point and verify a new strategy with evidence.
home.userDeveloperDescription: Locate the first meaningful failure without reading every raw event.
home.userQualityDescription: Compare attempts using repeatable rules instead of subjective impressions.
home.journeyDescription: The showcase follows the action a product team takes after an agent returns the wrong result.
home.journey.failureDescription: Summarize what the agent tried and where the task stopped.
home.journey.causeDescription: Identify repeated work that produced no new state or result.
home.journey.retryDescription: Recover from a safe point without changing the original record.
home.journey.verifyDescription: Check the fix, regressions and delivery cost with the same evidence.
home.decisionsTitle: The product decisions behind the flow
home.decisionsDescription: The interface is designed around trust, recoverability and clear verification rather than a single opaque score.
home.decision.evidenceDescription: Every diagnosis and verification result links back to the recorded operation that supports it.
home.decision.immutableDescription: A recovery creates a separate child attempt. It cannot rewrite the original run or comparison baseline.
home.decision.deterministicDescription: Tests, change scope and safety rules are evaluated deterministically before any model-based judgment.
home.resultsTitle: Targets and verified results stay separate
home.resultsDescription: The north-star metric is a verified-fix completion rate. Current claims are limited to reproducible product and engineering checks.
home.roleDescription: I led the product definition, user flow, interaction design, system architecture and full-stack implementation of AgentScope.
home.roleDisclosure: AI assisted implementation and review. Product decisions, scope control and final verification remained human-owned.
home.finalTitle: See the product decision, not every dashboard control
home.finalDescription: The guided story stays simple. The complete trace remains available when a technical reviewer wants to inspect the evidence.
launcher.title: See why an agent failed, fork the evidence, verify the fix.
launcher.description: A code-repair agent reads files, searches symbols, patches source and runs tests. AgentScope captures every decision and proves whether the child run actually improved.
launcher.executeDescription: The server owns the workspace, test command and tool allowlist. Models can select actions but never arbitrary shell commands.

case.metaDescription: How AgentScope traces a stalled code-repair Agent, forks an immutable Checkpoint and verifies the Child Run with deterministic evidence.
case.title: Designing a clearer way to debug agent failures
case.description: A product case about turning a dense execution trace into a guided path from failed outcome to verified recovery.
case.imageAlt: AgentScope guided product demonstration from failed run to verified fix
case.caption: One Projection drives Trace, Diagnostics, Compare and Eval.
case.failureTitle: The Parent did work, but made no progress
case.failureDescription: Tool names and inputs alone can mislabel a legitimate retry. AgentScope adds Workspace and test-result hashes to the call signature. Three identical test calls with unchanged state become a deterministic no-progress finding.
case.hashUnchanged: Workspace Hash + result Hash stayed unchanged
case.forkTitle: Forking is a state transition, not a retry button
case.forkDescription: A Checkpoint records the Fixture version, accumulated Patch, tool version and Workspace Snapshot reference. Fork restores that state into a Child Workspace. Parent events and Artifacts remain immutable, so comparison evidence cannot be rewritten by the recovery attempt.
case.childFlow: restore Snapshot → new strategy → verified test
case.securityTitle: The model chooses actions. The server owns authority.
case.securityDescription: The public deployment only serves recorded evidence. Local sandbox execution is restricted to one built-in scenario and fails closed when its dependencies are unavailable.
case.security.workspaceReason: A Child restores state without writing to Parent.
case.security.patchReason: Out-of-scope files are rejected before mutation.
case.security.testsReason: Models never provide arbitrary Shell commands.
case.security.runtimeReason: CPU, memory and execution time stay bounded.
case.verificationTitle: Verification stays attached to Trace evidence
case.verificationDescription: Compare reports resolved errors, regressions and trade-offs. Eval uses versioned deterministic rules for test success, Patch scope, replay safety and loop efficiency. Every claim links back to its supporting Span.
case.boundaryTitle: Why arbitrary repositories are out of scope
case.boundaryDescription: Safe execution of unknown repositories requires stronger isolation, supply-chain controls, tenancy, retention policies and an asynchronous Worker plane. The portfolio keeps one constrained scenario so its security claims remain honest and verifiable.
case.productCaption: The guided story leads with the product decision. The complete trace remains available as evidence.
case.problemDescription: Agent teams often receive a wrong final result and a large event log. Neither explains the smallest useful next action: where progress stopped and how to test a better strategy safely.
case.userDescription: An agent product or engineering owner who needs to explain a failed run, coordinate a fix and defend the result to a reviewer.
case.jobStatement: When an agent fails, help me find the first actionable cause, create a safe new attempt and prove whether the result improved.
case.journeyTitle: The solution follows the user's decision path
case.journeyDescription: The interface reveals only the information required for the current decision. Technical detail becomes available on demand.
case.journey.failureDescription: See the task, attempted actions and first meaningful failure.
case.journey.causeDescription: Explain repeated work with no state or result change.
case.journey.retryDescription: Create a separate attempt from a complete recovery point.
case.journey.verifyDescription: Compare success, regressions and delivery cost.
case.decisionsDescription: Each choice trades breadth or simplicity for stronger user trust and a clearer demonstration.
case.decision.evidenceDescription: A conclusion must link back to the operation that supports it. The interface starts with a plain-language summary and keeps raw IDs available.
case.decision.evidenceTradeoff: This adds trace structure, but avoids an unexplainable overall score.
case.decision.historyDescription: The original run stays immutable. A child attempt restores state from a recovery point and becomes independently comparable.
case.decision.historyTradeoff: Storage and comparison are more complex, but the baseline remains trustworthy.
case.decision.scope: One safe scenario before arbitrary repositories
case.decision.scopeDescription: The portfolio executes one built-in code-repair case with server-owned tools, files and tests.
case.decision.scopeTradeoff: The demo is narrower, but every safety claim remains honest and reproducible.
case.resultsTitle: Product targets and verified results are different claims
case.resultsDescription: The north-star metric defines future product success. The current portfolio only reports results that can be reproduced today.
case.metric.targetLabel: Product target, not live adoption data
case.deliverableTitle: A decision-ready output, not another dashboard
case.deliverableDescription: The final product brief translates execution evidence into a shared account of the failure, recovery choice, verified outcome and remaining limits.
case.deliverable.productDescription: Can explain what failed, why the recovery path was chosen and which product claim is actually verified.
case.deliverable.engineeringDescription: Can jump from each conclusion to the exact operation and inspect the full execution record when needed.
case.deliverable.qualityDescription: Can review deterministic checks, regressions and safety boundaries without relying on a model-generated score.
case.roleDescription: I led problem framing, requirements, product flow, interaction design, scope decisions, system architecture and full-stack implementation.
case.roleDisclosure: AI assisted coding and review. I retained ownership of product judgment, architecture choices, testing and release acceptance.
case.technicalTitle: Technical depth supports the product claim
case.technicalDescription: The public story is simple, but the underlying evidence, recovery and safety behavior remain inspectable by a technical reviewer.
case.technical.checkpoint: A complete checkpoint restores workspace state into a separate child without changing the parent.
case.technical.sandbox: The local sandbox uses an offline, non-root container and server-owned file and command allowlists.
case.technical.evaluation: Deterministic evaluation checks test success, change scope, repetition and replay safety.
case.productBoundaryDescription: The project does not claim arbitrary repository execution, production adoption or enterprise governance. The next product step is validating the guided workflow with target users before expanding runtime breadth.
